raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

Add matching PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 release wheels for Linux x86_64 and aarch64. The release workflow currently builds only PyTorch 2.8/CUDA 12.9 wheels. Publishing matching wheels lets users download the PyTorch extension instead of needing a local C++/CUDA build.

Also preserve checkout space on runners where `/mnt` shares the root filesystem. Pooling both paths consumes the space needed to clone the source dependencies. The observed v2.20.2 ARM release job failed during CUTLASS checkout with `fatal: write error: No space left on device`.

The install smoke check needs `transformer-engine` and its core wheel from PyPI, and a GitHub release can precede those uploads. This happened for v2.14, v2.14.1, v2.16, and v2.20.2. The check now reports a workflow warning and continues in that case, so upload order cannot stop a release from publishing the new wheels.

Fixes #3310

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

- Add Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 builds for both architectures.
- Add SM100 to the build image architecture list and install the CUDA development packages needed for the build. The PyTorch extension has no CUDA sources, so its Blackwell kernels come from the `transformer_engine_cu13` core wheel.
- Preserve checkout space when `/mnt` shares the root filesystem.
- Keep compiler output visible and fail the job when the build fails or times out.
- Check wheel tags before upload and run install/import smoke checks for the new builds. Skip the smoke check with a workflow warning when PyPI does not have the release packages for the platform.

## Before and after

| Outcome | Before | With this change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Defined Python 3.12 release builds | 2 configurations: PyTorch 2.8/CUDA 12.9 on x86_64 and aarch64 | 4 configurations: retain those builds and add PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 on both architectures |
| Existing ARM PyTorch 2.8/CUDA 12.9 build on TE v2.20.2 | [CUTLASS checkout failed](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/37374633284/job/111989480609) with about 32 MiB free on the root filesystem | [Native ARM validation](https://github.com/bvolpato/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/38966139162/job/117201392544) skipped pooling on the shared-filesystem layout, built a `linux_aarch64` wheel, and passed installation/import checks |

The validation also built and imported the [new ARM PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 wheel](https://github.com/bvolpato/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/38966139162/job/117201395453). Both ARM build configurations used the same TE v2.20.2 source as the failed release job.

## Validation

Repository hooks and shell checks found no new problems. Actionlint reported only existing workflow diagnostics. Rerun the hooks with `pre-commit run --all-files`.

A [release matrix run](https://github.com/bvolpato/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/41271222435) used this PR's composite action and the release matrix on `ubuntu-22.04` and `ubuntu-22.04-arm`. It built PyTorch 2.8/CUDA 12.9 and PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 wheels from the `v2.21` tag on both architectures. That version is not on PyPI, so the two new builds reported the warning, skipped the smoke check, and still produced wheels with the expected names. An x86_64 PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 build from v2.20.2 in the same run installed and imported its wheel. The x86_64 runner also reported that `/mnt` shares the root filesystem, so this layout is no longer specific to ARM. In a [separate run](https://github.com/bvolpato/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/41280270251) of the previous disk pooling steps, the x86_64 job left 32 MiB free on root and still checked out v2.21 with 1.3 GiB left. The ARM runner stopped during checkout with `No space left on device`.

The wheel from that v2.20.2 build also ran on one NVIDIA B200 (driver 580.95.05) with no CUDA toolkit and no system cuDNN on the host. It used PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130 and `transformer_engine_cu13==2.20.2` from PyPI. TE took its no-toolkit loading path, and every loaded CUDA library came from the virtual environment (cuDNN 9.19, cuBLAS 13.1, and NVRTC 13.0). An MXFP8 `Linear` forward and backward pass and an MXFP8 `GroupedLinear` forward pass ran. `test_sanity.py`, `test_quantized_tensor.py`, `tests/pytorch/mxfp8`, `test_grouped_linear.py`, `test_float8_current_scaling_exact.py`, and `test_numerics.py` from the v2.20.2 tag found no failures. `test_numerics.py` needed `NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0`: without it, FP32 cases differ from the PyTorch reference because TE selects TF32 for pure FP32 GEMM, and source builds of current `main` show the same differences. The file name that `get_wheel_url()` computes from the PyPI sdist with this PyTorch matches the built asset.

`test_float8_blockwise_gemm_exact.py` skipped every case, so it adds no coverage. GPU execution on GB200 has not been tested, so the aarch64 wheel is validated only through build, install, and import.

The before/after table links to an earlier native ARM run, which predates the PyPI timing change. Its CUDA 12 build required an unchanged retry after an external PPA returned HTTP 503, and its before/after runs used different runner instances. Build time and install time were not benchmarked. The release workflow does not run on PRs, so the `release` event and the asset upload step were not exercised. The `v2.21` tag does not contain this workflow change, so a release event for that tag uses its existing matrix.

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge.

Summary

Adds PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 release wheels for both Linux architectures. - Release builds add PyTorch 2.11 and CUDA 13 wheels for both Linux architectures. - Wheel builds skip disk pooling when `/` and `/mnt` share a device. - Release builds check wheel tags and import wheels when matching packages are available. No new actionable issues were found. The earlier unnumbered thread concerns a dedicated ARM job that is no longer present; no duplicate comment is needed. Reviews (6) · Last reviewed commit: ["\[CI\] Keep wheel uploads independent of P..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/93875c1ab5eba1fccdafb143462c6d4d075f4c13) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

@fheinecke, would you mind taking a look at this when you get a chance? The PR is green and mergeable, and the previous review concern is resolved. It adds PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 release wheels for x86_64 and aarch64, with wheel/tag validation and a driverless import check. If someone else owns this release path now, happy to redirect.

@ksivaman, could you take a look at this, or point me to current owner for PyTorch release-wheel workflow? It extends #2138 to PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 on x86_64 and aarch64. Checks are green and only review thread is resolved.

I rechecked this against [v2.20.2](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/releases/tag/v2.20.2): the PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 aarch64 asset is still missing. The [ARM release job](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/37374633284/job/111989480609) fails with `fatal: write error: No space left on device` during checkout because disk pooling leaves only 32 MiB on the shared root filesystem. I pushed `592be137` to skip pooling when `/mnt` shares that filesystem. Local layout and build/matrix validation pass, and the PR checks are green. Could someone review the updated release-wheel changes? Native aarch64 compilation and import still need validation on an ARM runner.

@fheinecke, would you mind taking a look at this when you get a chance? It adds PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 release wheels for x86_64 and aarch64 and fixes the ARM checkout space issue. Checks are green, with native ARM build/import validation still outstanding. If someone else owns the release workflow, happy to redirect.

Some data from the release runs that may help review. Since v2.15, which was the last release with an aarch64 PyTorch wheel attached, the `ubuntu-22.04-arm` job has failed on every release, and not always for the same reason:

| release | arm job failure |
|---|---|
| v2.16, v2.16.1 | logs no longer available (#3309 quotes `No space left on device` for v2.16.1) |
| v2.17 | checkout: `No space left on device` while cloning `3rdparty/cutlass` |
| v2.17.1 | build: `RuntimeError: Error compiling objects for extension`; the compiler error itself is not in the log |
| v2.18 | build: same as v2.17.1 |
| v2.19 | checkout: same as v2.17 |
| v2.20.2 | checkout: same as v2.17 |

So the checkout fix here covers v2.17, v2.19 and v2.20.2. The two compile failures in v2.17.1 and v2.18 cannot be diagnosed from the logs, because the build output went through `| tail -n 1`. With this PR's logging change, a native ARM run should show whether that failure still happens after the disk fix. It might be worth checking before the next release.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Thanks for checking the release history. I ran this branch's build scripts on native ARM against v2.20.2, and the existing CUDA 12 and new CUDA 13 wheels built and imported successfully ([run](https://github.com/bvolpato/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/38966139162)). The first CUDA 12 attempt hit a temporary PPA 503, then passed unchanged on retry. I still can't identify the older compiler errors from the truncated logs.

Rechecked this PR at `6ab002a58a85d8e5dd5a6e44626258f507fa9ce7`. The current diff has no outstanding review feedback or merge conflicts. DCO, pre-commit, label, and Greptile checks pass.

The [native ARM validation](https://github.com/bvolpato/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/38966139162) built and imported both PyTorch 2.8/CUDA 12.9 and PyTorch 2.11/CUDA 13 wheels using build files matching this head. That validates wheel construction and imports, not GPU execution.

Documentation, License, Lint, and Minimum Supported Versions remain `action_required` with no jobs. I tried rerunning [Documentation](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/actions/runs/39086655251), but GitHub returned `Must have admin rights to Repository`.

Could a maintainer approve the gated workflows and review the release-wheel changes? I found no additional code change needed for this PR.

**Mutable release action references** The new ARM release job invokes `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/upload-release-asset@v1` through mutable tags. If either upstream tag is repointed or compromised, changed action code runs against the build workspace and release-writing token, exposing the wheel artifact and release to tampering; pin both new references to full commit SHAs. **How this was verified:** The new checkout and upload steps use mutable tags, and the upload action receives `GITHUB_TOKEN` plus the release upload URL.

inline_comments.body: **Mutable release action references** The new ARM release job invokes `actions/checkout@v4` and `actions/upload-release-asset@v1` through mutable tags.
